abstract_sentences.text: Estimating probability density and its score from samples remains a core problem in generative modeling, Bayesian inference, and kinetic theory.
abstract_sentences.link_to_next: The scope establishes why estimator alternatives matter.

evidence.anchor: Estimating probability density and its score

abstract_sentences.text: Existing methods are bifurcated: classical kernel density estimators (KDE) generalize across distributions but suffer from the curse of dimensionality, while neural score-matching models achieve high precision but require retraining for every target distribution.
abstract_sentences.link_to_next: The bifurcation licenses a new estimator.

evidence.anchor: Existing methods are bifurcated

abstract_sentences.text: We introduce DiScoFormer (Density and Score Transformer), an equivariant Transformer that maps i.i.d. samples to both density values and score vectors.
abstract_sentences.link_to_next: The following sentence differentiates its learning target.

evidence.anchor: maps i.i.d. samples to both density values and score vectors

abstract_sentences.text: Unlike score matching, which learns a fixed function R^d → R^d for a single distribution, DiScoFormer learns a sequence-to-sequence operator that generalizes across distributions and sample sizes without retraining.
abstract_sentences.link_to_next: It leads to theory and mechanism evidence.

evidence.anchor: generalizes across distributions and sample sizes

abstract_sentences.text: Analytically, we prove that self-attention can recover normalized KDE, establishing it as a functional generalization of kernel methods; empirically, individual attention heads learn multi-scale, kernel-like behaviors.
abstract_sentences.link_to_next: It supplies the premise for the final performance/use claim.

evidence.anchor: self-attention can recover normalized KDE

abstract_sentences.text: The model outperforms KDE for density and score estimation, and provides a plug-in score oracle for score-debiased KDE, Fisher information computation, and Fokker–Planck-type PDEs.

evidence.anchor: outperforms KDE for density and score estimation
foundational problem in statistical inference

final_judgment.single_storyline: DiScoFormer frames density/score estimation as an equivariant sample-to-operator problem, proves a constructive attention–KDE bridge, and evaluates that learned oracle across synthetic estimation and plug-in uses.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: Problem tension, symmetry target, whitening/cross-attention mechanism, main expressivity statements, training/data setup, Tables 1–6, applications and three explicit limitations.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Proof details, conditional GMM-to-non-GMM theory, full attention visualizations, score-matching comparison and runtime qualification move to pp. 14–21; critical theory conditions require those pages.
final_judgment.best_pattern: A constructive mechanism statement is followed by a mechanism-facing visualization, a directly aligned whitening ablation, then downstream uses of the same oracle.
final_judgment.largest_gap: Most results omit seed/replication/dispersion information; OOD/high-dimensional evidence remains synthetic and bounded; no asymptotic guarantee is available.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a universal estimator claim, connect the architecture to a known estimator with a constructible mapping, then test the implicated component and a downstream task using the same object.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: Use this pattern where a structural mapping exists. When it does not, use falsifiable predictions or direct counterfactual tests rather than treating qualitative attention plots as proof.
final_judgment.self_sufficiency: Main text supplies the narrative and decision tables; Appendix A/B is still required to audit the exact construction and its assumptions.
